+### Enabling automatic retry with `init.retry`
+
+<!-- YAML
+added: REPLACEME
+-->
+
+By default `fetch()` surfaces every network failure to the caller, matching
+the WHATWG Fetch Standard. This can be inconvenient in practice: keep-alive
+sockets closed between requests, transient `ECONNRESET`s, and transient
+`5xx` responses all cost a full application-level retry. The `init.retry`
+option opts into undici's [`RetryHandler`][] without having to replace the
+dispatcher.
+
+```mjs
+import { fetch } from 'undici'
+
+// Enable retry with RetryHandler defaults: ECONNRESET, UND_ERR_SOCKET,
+// and 429/5xx are retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff.
+const response = await fetch('https://example.com', { retry: true })
+```
+
+Pass a [`RetryOptions`][] object to tune the behaviour:
+
+```mjs
+await fetch('https://example.com', {
+  retry: {
+    maxRetries: 3,
+    minTimeout: 500,
+    maxTimeout: 5_000,
+    timeoutFactor: 2,
+    errorCodes: ['ECONNRESET', 'UND_ERR_SOCKET'],
+    statusCodes: [502, 503, 504]
+  }
+})
+```
+
+The option also round-trips through the `Request` constructor:
+
+```mjs
+const req = new Request('https://example.com', { retry: true })
+const response = await fetch(req)
+```
+
+Setting `retry: false` is identical to omitting the option — both preserve
+the WHATWG default behaviour. The option composes with `init.dispatcher`:
+retry wraps the dispatcher the user supplied (or the global dispatcher
+when none is supplied), so proxy agents, mock agents, and custom pools
+all keep working with retry on top.
+
+Stateful request bodies (readable streams, `AsyncIterable`) cannot be
+replayed, so the first retry rejects with `UND_ERR_REQ_RETRY` — this matches
+[`RetryHandler`][]'s existing contract.
+
+See [#3492](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/3492) for the design
+discussion.
+
+[`RetryHandler`]: ./RetryHandler.md
+[`RetryOptions`]: ./RetryHandler.md#parameter-retryoptions
+

+/**
+ * Wrap a dispatcher with RetryAgent when the user opted in via `init.retry`.
+ * Returning the original dispatcher when `retry` is undefined/false preserves
+ * the historical fetch behaviour of surfacing every network error — nothing
+ * runs through the retry path unless the caller explicitly asks for it.
+ *
+ * Opt-in shapes:
+ *   fetch(url, { retry: true })                  // RetryHandler defaults
+ *   fetch(url, { retry: { maxRetries: 5, ... } }) // forwarded to RetryHandler
+ *   fetch(url, { retry: false })                 // explicit opt-out
+ *
+ * The dispatcher is always a fresh RetryAgent so retry state stays per-request.
+ *
+ * @param {import('../../..').Dispatcher | undefined} dispatcher
+ * @param {boolean | import('../../..').RetryHandler.RetryOptions | undefined} retry
+ * @returns {import('../../..').Dispatcher | undefined}
+ * @see {@link https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/3492}
+ */
+function resolveRetryDispatcher (dispatcher, retry) {
+  if (retry === undefined || retry === false) return dispatcher
+  const inner = dispatcher ?? getGlobalDispatcher()
+  const options = retry === true ? {} : retry
+  return new RetryAgent(inner, options)
+}
+

+'use strict'
+
+// Regression test for https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/3492
+//
+// fetch previously had no way to opt into the RetryHandler infrastructure
+// that undici has shipped for direct Dispatcher consumers since v5.28. The
+// `init.retry` option exposes that infrastructure to fetch callers:
+//
+//   fetch(url, { retry: true })             // RetryHandler defaults
+//   fetch(url, { retry: { maxRetries: 5 } }) // forwarded to RetryHandler
+//   fetch(url, { retry: false })            // explicit opt-out
+//   fetch(url)                              // historical behaviour
+//
+// Tests are deterministic (counting server hits) rather than relying on
+// the exact closed-connection timing from the original repro, which varies
+// across Node versions. The original race-recovery case lives in its own
+// test so it does not block the suite when Node itself has fixed the race.
+
+const { test, after } = require('node:test')
+const { createServer } = require('node:http')
+const { once } = require('node:events')
+const assert = require('node:assert')
+
+const { fetch, Request, Agent } = require('../..')
+const { closeServerAsPromise } = require('../utils/node-http')
+
+test('fetch(url) without init.retry does not retry on 5xx (preserves historical behaviour)', async () => {
+  let hits = 0
+  const server = createServer({ joinDuplicateHeaders: true }, (req, res) => {
+    hits++
+    res.statusCode = 500
+    res.end('busy')
+  })
+  after(closeServerAsPromise(server))
+
+  server.listen(0)
+  await once(server, 'listening')
+  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`
+
+  const res = await fetch(url)
+  assert.strictEqual(res.status, 500)
+  assert.strictEqual(hits, 1, 'default fetch must not retry')
+})
+
+test('fetch(url, { retry: true }) opts into RetryHandler defaults', async () => {
+  let hits = 0
+  const server = createServer({ joinDuplicateHeaders: true }, (req, res) => {
+    hits++
+    res.statusCode = 500
+    res.end('busy')
+  })
+  after(closeServerAsPromise(server))
+
+  server.listen(0)
+  await once(server, 'listening')
+  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`
+
+  // RetryHandler defaults include status 500 and maxRetries 5.
+  // After retries are exhausted it throws UND_ERR_REQ_RETRY — the correctness
+  // signal here is that the server was hit more than once.
+  await assert.rejects(fetch(url, { retry: true }), (err) => {
+    assert.strictEqual(err.cause?.code, 'UND_ERR_REQ_RETRY')
+    return true
+  })
+  assert.ok(hits > 1, `retry: true must retry; server was hit ${hits} times`)
+})
+
+test('fetch init.retry forwards maxRetries verbatim to RetryHandler', async () => {
+  let hits = 0
+  const server = createServer({ joinDuplicateHeaders: true }, (req, res) => {
+    hits++
+    res.statusCode = 500
+    res.end('busy')
+  })
+  after(closeServerAsPromise(server))
+
+  server.listen(0)
+  await once(server, 'listening')
+  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`
+
+  await assert.rejects(
+    fetch(url, {
+      retry: {
+        maxRetries: 2,
+        minTimeout: 1,
+        maxTimeout: 10,
+        timeoutFactor: 1
+      }
+    }),
+    (err) => {
+      assert.strictEqual(err.cause?.code, 'UND_ERR_REQ_RETRY')
+      return true
+    }
+  )
+  assert.strictEqual(hits, 3, '1 initial + 2 retries = 3 server hits')
+})
+
+test('fetch init.retry = false explicitly disables retry', async () => {
+  let hits = 0
+  const server = createServer({ joinDuplicateHeaders: true }, (req, res) => {
+    hits++
+    res.statusCode = 500
+    res.end('busy')
+  })
+  after(closeServerAsPromise(server))
+
+  server.listen(0)
+  await once(server, 'listening')
+  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`
+
+  const res = await fetch(url, { retry: false })
+  assert.strictEqual(res.status, 500)
+  assert.strictEqual(hits, 1, 'retry: false must not retry even if default changes')
+})
+
+test('fetch init.retry respects custom statusCodes override', async () => {
+  let hits = 0
+  const server = createServer({ joinDuplicateHeaders: true }, (req, res) => {
+    hits++
+    res.statusCode = 500 // not in our custom allowlist below
+    res.end('busy')
+  })
+  after(closeServerAsPromise(server))
+
+  server.listen(0)
+  await once(server, 'listening')
+  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`
+
+  // User says "only retry 503, not 500" — the 500 must surface as a response
+  // without being retried.
+  const res = await fetch(url, {
+    retry: {
+      maxRetries: 3,
+      minTimeout: 1,
+      maxTimeout: 10,
+      timeoutFactor: 1,
+      statusCodes: [503]
+    }
+  })
+  assert.strictEqual(res.status, 500)
+  assert.strictEqual(hits, 1, 'statusCodes override honoured — no retry')
+})
+
+test('Request constructor accepts retry and fetch(req) picks it up', async () => {
+  let hits = 0
+  const server = createServer({ joinDuplicateHeaders: true }, (req, res) => {
+    hits++
+    res.statusCode = 500
+    res.end('busy')
+  })
+  after(closeServerAsPromise(server))
+
+  server.listen(0)
+  await once(server, 'listening')
+  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`
+
+  const req = new Request(url, {
+    retry: { maxRetries: 1, minTimeout: 1, maxTimeout: 10, timeoutFactor: 1 }
+  })
+  await assert.rejects(fetch(req), (err) => {
+    assert.strictEqual(err.cause?.code, 'UND_ERR_REQ_RETRY')
+    return true
+  })
+  assert.strictEqual(hits, 2, 'Request-level retry: 1 initial + 1 retry')
+})
+
+test('Request.clone() preserves the retry option', async () => {
+  let hits = 0
+  const server = createServer({ joinDuplicateHeaders: true }, (req, res) => {
+    hits++
+    res.statusCode = 500
+    res.end('busy')
+  })
+  after(closeServerAsPromise(server))
+
+  server.listen(0)
+  await once(server, 'listening')
+  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`
+
+  const req = new Request(url, {
+    retry: { maxRetries: 1, minTimeout: 1, maxTimeout: 10, timeoutFactor: 1 }
+  })
+  const clone = req.clone()
+  await assert.rejects(fetch(clone), (err) => {
+    assert.strictEqual(err.cause?.code, 'UND_ERR_REQ_RETRY')
+    return true
+  })
+  assert.strictEqual(hits, 2, 'clone must inherit retry: 1 initial + 1 retry')
+})
+
+test('fetch init.retry wraps a user-provided dispatcher instead of the global one', async () => {
+  let hits = 0
+  const server = createServer({ joinDuplicateHeaders: true }, (req, res) => {
+    hits++
+    res.statusCode = 500
+    res.end('busy')
+  })
+  after(closeServerAsPromise(server))
+
+  server.listen(0)
+  await once(server, 'listening')
+  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`
+
+  // Custom dispatcher — if the retry wrap swallowed it, no requests would
+  // reach the server at all (dispatchers are not interchangeable with the
+  // global one for arbitrary origins). Server hits > 0 proves wrap composed.
+  const dispatcher = new Agent({ keepAliveTimeout: 1 })
+  after(() => dispatcher.destroy())
+
+  await assert.rejects(
+    fetch(url, {
+      dispatcher,
+      retry: { maxRetries: 1, minTimeout: 1, maxTimeout: 10, timeoutFactor: 1 }
+    }),
+    (err) => {
+      assert.strictEqual(err.cause?.code, 'UND_ERR_REQ_RETRY')
+      return true
+    }
+  )
+  assert.strictEqual(hits, 2, 'custom dispatcher reached + retry applied on top')
+})
